x.Jeden opravdu volný den v týdnu monotónn: One truly free day a week knocks monotony down without changing anything in total load. The signal is sensitive to how the runner plans, not just how much they run.
x.Jednotlivé varovné příznaky mají samy o: Individual warning signs have weak predictive value on their own; the doctor's clinical judgement decides. The app determines nothing; it only pauses training and refers you to a doctor.
x.Kapacitu tkáně nelze měřit přímo; defici: Tissue capacity can't be measured directly; the deficit is only an indirect proxy from recovery markers.

x.Když jednotlivý trénink i týdenní součet: When both a single session and the weekly total fall below your capacity.

x.Lineární rozpad je zjednodušení; skutečn: Linear decay is a simplification; the actual tissue recovery time is individual.

x.Mechanistická úvaha. Generuje hypotézu,: Mechanistic reasoning. Generates a hypothesis, nothing more.
x.Metaanalýzy a běžecké kohorty ukazují, ž: Meta-analyses and running cohorts show that even small but repeated two-week increases in load precede injury — not just big jumps. It catches a creeping increase that the 7:28 ratio doesn't yet flag.
x.Místo na mapě těla neodliší kost od sval: A spot on the body map can't distinguish bone from muscle or tendon, so this is a precautionary rule.
x.Měření spánku z hodinek je nepřesné, zvl: Sleep measurement from the watch is imprecise, especially for stages. That's why the value can be overwritten manually.
x.Nad zhruba 5 % na aerobním běhu naznačuj: Above roughly 5 % on an aerobic run it suggests unresolved fatigue. Established in endurance monitoring.
x.Nad ~85 % po několika nocích klidnějšího: Above ~85 % after a few nights of calmer sleep.
x.Nespecifické. Rozlišit infekt od přetíže: Non-specific. An infection can't be told apart from overload without more data — so it is tied to the check-in.
x.Nižší kadence při srovnatelném tempu zna: A lower cadence at a comparable pace means a longer stride and longer ground contact — associated with higher impact and braking force. A drop vs your own norm is often an early sign of developing fatigue or a change in technique.

x.Návrat kadence k vlastní normě po několi: Cadence returns to your own norm after several runs in comparable conditions.
x.Návrat oscilace k vlastní normě po odleh: Oscillation returns to your own norm after easing off or adding strength work.
x.Návrat po přetížení kosti se řídí úplnou: Return after bone overload is guided by complete absence of pain (Warden et al., 2014), unlike tendon, where pain up to 5/10 is tolerated (Silbernagel et al., 2007).

x.Odborný komentář, ne systematický přehle: Expert commentary, not a systematic review. The app determines nothing; it only refers you to a physiotherapist.
x.Opírá se o malé studie, HRV reaguje i na: Based on small studies; HRV also reacts to many influences outside training.

After ascent returns below your capacity.
x.Po odpovědi „ne“ v dalším check-inu (pla: After answering “no” in the next check-in (applies today and tomorrow).
x.Po týdnu stabilního nebo sníženého objem: After a week of stable or reduced volume.
x.Pokles HRV proti vlastní normě je zavede: A drop in HRV vs your own norm is an established marker of incomplete recovery and autonomic stress. It is used as a modulator of the load axis, not as a standalone reason to intervene.
x.Poměr HI zátěže se vrátí k ~1 po pár dne: The HI load ratio returns to ~1 after a few days without hard runs.
x.Poměr klesne pod 1,2 po dvou týdnech pra: The ratio falls below 1.2 after two weeks of a more regular routine.
x.Poměr klesne pod 1,2 po týdnu pravidelné: The ratio falls below 1.2 after a week of regular measurement.
x.Poměr klesne pod 1,3 po týdnu stabilizov: The ratio falls below 1.3 after a week of stabilised volume.
x.Poměr se vrátí do 0,7–1,3 po dvou týdnec: The ratio returns to 0.7–1.3 after two weeks of stable volume.
x.Prahy jsou pracovní předpoklady, ne vali: The thresholds are working assumptions, not validated criteria.
x.Prudké zrychlení je jiný mechanismus než: A sharp increase in speed is a different mechanism from an increase in distance — Nielsen 2014 maps pace jumps more to the Achilles / plantar fascia / shin, while distance maps to the knee/shin.
x.Prudký nárůst tvrdé práce na nízké chron: A sharp increase in hard work on a low chronic base of hard work is, according to the team's evidence, riskier than the same increase in total load at easy intensity. It separates intensity from mere volume.
x.Předchozí zranění je konzistentně nejsil: A previous injury is consistently the strongest predictor of further injury across studies.
x.Předchozí zranění je nejrobustnější rizi: A previous injury is the most robust risk factor across the literature (Hulme 2017; van Poppel 2021); recurrence in the same area is its strongest manifestation.
x.Retrospektivní a subjektivní. Běžci před: Retrospective and subjective. Before a race, runners systematically underestimate it.
x.Riziko zranění po prudkém nárůstu zátěže: Injury risk after a sharp increase in load peaks 1–4 weeks AFTER it, not on the day of the jump (IOC consensus 2016; the effect lasts up to a month). The status therefore stays elevated until the adaptation catches up.
x.Roste-li rozptyl kontaktu se zemí kolem: If the spread of ground contact around your own norm grows from run to run, it is often an early signal of neuromuscular fatigue or compensation — it shows up before the average shifts. Gait variability is an established marker in movement pathology.
x.Rozchod mezi vnitřní a vnější zátěží býv: A divergence between internal and external load is often a sign of fatigue (Bourdon et al., 2017; Halson, 2014).
x.Rozptyl se vrátí k baseline po pár konzi: The spread returns to baseline after a few consistent runs in comparable conditions.
x.Roztříštěný spánek (nízká efektivita, WA: Fragmented sleep (low efficiency, WASO) is associated with a higher risk of musculoskeletal injury beyond the number of hours slept — cohorts of adolescents and elite athletes.

x.Sebehodnocená bolest je nejsilnější jedn: Self-reported pain is the strongest single predictor and the only grade A signal the platform has continuously available. Biomechanics complements it, it doesn't replace it.
x.Sebehodnocená bolest zůstává nejsilnější: Self-reported pain remains the strongest single predictor. Repeated reporting of the same spot after sessions is clinically more significant than a one-off high value in the weekly check-in, because it captures a pattern tied to a specific type of load.
x.Seběh je excentrická zátěž: nárazové síl: Downhill running is an eccentric load: impact forces grow with gradient (Gottschall & Kram 2005) and muscle damage is greatest at the first unfamiliar dose — repeated exposure protects (repeated-bout effect, McHugh 2003). That's why it is measured against YOUR recent descent dose, not in absolute terms.
x.Sekundární analýza randomizované studie: A secondary analysis of a randomised trial with more than 800 recreational runners showed that gait asymmetry in spatial and kinetic variables doesn't increase the risk of lower-limb injury. The often-cited figure of a 75% injury rate above 10 % asymmetry comes from military basic training and doesn't transfer to recreational runners. The platform therefore doesn't flag absolute asymmetry — only its change vs your own norm. Subtle shifts in asymmetry, including a reversal of the ratio of reaction forces between limbs, have been observed before bone stress injury in collegiate runners.
x.Signál zmizí, když se VR ve stejných pod: The signal disappears when VR returns to within ±1 SD under the same conditions for three sessions.
x.Silně závislá na typu tréninku v předcho: Strongly dependent on the type of training in the preceding days.
x.Skok v délce jednoho běhu proti nejdelší: A jump in single-run distance vs the longest run of the previous 30 days is a dose-dependent risk factor in a cohort of 5,205 runners (Frandsen 2025); a sharp weekly increase (> 30 %) is linked to some types of injury (Nielsen 2014). Capacity is what you have demonstrably managed without problems.
x.Smíšená nebo vznikající evidence — signá: Mixed or emerging evidence — a signal, not proof.
x.Spánek pod vlastní normou opakovaně sniž: Sleep repeatedly below your own norm lowers load tolerance and impairs soft-tissue recovery.
x.Stabilní nebo rostoucí trend po dvou týd: A stable or rising trend after two weeks.
x.Stejné příznaky mohou mít mnoho příčin (: The same symptoms can have many causes (load, sleep, stress, nutrition, illness), so it pays to discuss them with a professional rather than looking for a single cause (Jeukendrup et al., 2024).
x.Stoupání zvyšuje zatížení lýtka a Achill: Climbing increases the load on the calf and Achilles tendon and the metabolic demand (Minetti 2002).
x.Stupeň C — jde o rozšíření zavedeného HR: Grade C — an extension of the established HRV signal with a new axis, not a separately prospectively validated metric. Sensitive to irregular measurement (missed nights).
x.Stupeň C — logická kombinace dvou alread: Grade C — a logical combination of two already existing signals (date + load), not a separately validated predictor. It doesn't assess the quality of the training plan, only its timing.
x.Stupeň C — mechanistická úvaha, ne prosp: Grade C — mechanistic reasoning, not a prospectively validated threshold. With real data it depends on the density of GPS/elevation records in the export; with demo data the profile is synthesised from the run's actual total elevation, not measured.
x.Stupeň C — nejslabší kanál, proto nejniž: Grade C — the weakest channel, hence the lowest weight.
x.Stupeň C — plíživý nárůst je normální so: Grade C — a creeping increase is a normal part of building fitness; it is risky mainly in combination with suppressed recovery or symptoms. On its own it is not a reason to intervene.
x.Stupeň C — čistě subjektivní, kolísá s n: Grade C — purely subjective, varies with mood and context. Supplementary, not a standalone reason to intervene.
x.Stupeň C, čistě sebehodnocené. Závisí na: Grade C, purely self-rated. It depends on how honestly and regularly the runner fills in the ratings, and how well they can tell stiffness from muscle soreness.
x.Stupeň C. Kadence přirozeně kolísá s tem: Grade C. Cadence naturally varies with pace and terrain — so it is compared only within matching profiles, not against a population norm. Stride length is the other side of the same coin, so it isn't counted separately.
x.Stupeň C. Mechanisticky dává smysl, pros: Grade C. It makes mechanistic sense; prospective validation for injury risk is weak. Sensitive to pace and terrain — hence per profile.
x.Stupeň C. Mechanisticky to dává smysl, p: Grade C. It makes mechanistic sense; there is no prospective validation. At the same time it is the metric that moves first.
x.Stupeň C. Ovlivněno počasím, motivací i: Grade C. Affected by the weather, motivation and how the last race went.
x.Stupeň C: silný mechanismus, málo prospe: Grade C: a strong mechanism, few prospective injury data. Without an elevation profile the gradient is estimated from your other runs.
x.Stále je to proxy kumulativní zátěže tká: It is still a proxy for cumulative tissue load, not a direct measurement of it; repeated smaller jumps in the same week are captured rather by creep and the fading memory. Internal load is missing without a heart-rate curve.
x.Subjektivní únava bývá časný signál — ro: Subjective fatigue is often an early signal — it rises before HRV or resting heart rate move. Only the last few days are taken (the daily check-in is a 'today' signal); persistent problems go through the weekly OSTRC.
x.Sám body nepřidává (od railway#91). Sniž: Adds no points by itself (since railway#91). It lowers load tolerance and multiplies the signal “Pain at the site of a previous injury”.
x.Tempo z GPS je zašuměné; nerozlišuje int: GPS pace is noisy; it doesn't distinguish intervals from a continuous acceleration.
x.Tep kolísá mezi dny až o 6,5 %, proto pr: Heart rate varies between days by up to 6.5 %, hence the average of several runs. Elevation is converted using the equation of Minetti et al. (2002), which describes an average runner.
x.Trend se srovná, jakmile se doplní síla: The trend levels out once calf and glute strength is added or the share of long runs is reduced.
x.Tyto projevy jsou typické pro únavové př: These signs are typical of bone stress from overload and should be assessed regardless of the pain number (Warden et al., 2014).

x.Vertikální oscilace sama o sobě je špatn: Vertical oscillation on its own is a poor unit — whoever lengthens their stride raises VO without losing economy. The normalised vertical ratio solves this. Lower vertical oscillation of the trunk is associated with better running economy and a lower vertical loading rate, which is a recognised risk factor for lower-limb injury. A rising VR in comparable conditions therefore suggests a loss of elastic push-off before it starts to hurt.

x.Vysoká svalová bolestivost po tréninku j: High muscle soreness after training as a supplementary signal of incomplete recovery.
x.Vyšší HRV není automaticky dobrá zpráva,: Higher HRV isn't automatically good news; with functional overreaching it can also rise (Plews et al., 2014).
x.Vyšší vertikální oscilace znamená víc po: Higher vertical oscillation means more movement up/down instead of forward — less economical running and higher impact load per step. An increase vs your own norm at the same pace suggests worsening technique or fatigue.
x.Zachytí běžce, který nikdy nemá skutečně: It catches a runner who never has a genuinely easy day. High monotony at sufficient volume is a different failure mode from a volume jump — metrics based on volume alone can't see it.
x.Zařazení jednoho úplného volna a jednoho: Include one full rest day and one markedly shorter run each week.
x.Zmizí 14 dní po posledním označení dříve: Disappears 14 days after the last mark of a previously injured spot.

x.v0.4. Banisterův impulz-odezva model z v: v0.4. Banister's impulse-response model from the performance literature, carried over here as a complementary view of the EWMA ratio — it works better at low chronic load, where the ACWR ratio behaves unstably. A markedly negative balance means that acute load is persistently outpacing the capacity built.
x.v0.4. Doplňuje signál potlačené HRV o ji: v0.4. Complements the suppressed HRV signal with another axis: not how much HRV fell, but how unstable it is from day to day. Rising day-to-day variability without a drop in the mean is often an early marker of autonomic instability that the z-score of the mean alone would miss.
x.v0.4. Doplňuje spánkový dluh o jinou osu: v0.4. Complements sleep debt with another axis: not how much sleep is missing vs the average, but how irregular its duration is from day to day. Irregular sleep is associated with poorer load tolerance, also outside the running literature.
x.v0.5. Ztuhlost nohou před během je subje: v0.5. Leg stiffness before runs is a subjective signal of incomplete recovery, collected retrospectively when rating a run. On its own it is just another symptom — more interesting is the pattern where the runner trains at a high perceived effort despite reported stiffness: that suggests a reduced ability to listen to one's own body, not just fatigue itself.

x.Délka kroku (m). Kratší krok při stejném: Stride length (m). A shorter stride at the same pace = higher cadence and vice versa. What matters is the change against your baseline in comparable conditions.
x.Dnešní kapacita = kolik si dnes můžete d: Today's capacity = how much you can afford today so that: (1) the last 7 days don't exceed your weekly capacity — the same one shown in Load (capacity + 15 % margin, adjusted by readiness during the week), (2) this week stays on target for the cycle (90 / 100 / 110 / 55 %), (3) no single run exceeds the capacity of a single run, (4) the total load (heart rate × time from all activities) stays below the ceiling. The strictest of them applies — each channel shows which. When mechanics are above the threshold of 25, today shrinks further (volume −20 %, intensity and descent by half); when load is above the threshold, a recovery week follows. That way both axes stay below the threshold.
x.Doba kontaktu se zemí (ms) — jak dlouho: Ground contact time (ms) — how long the foot is on the ground. An increase against your baseline (at a comparable pace) suggests fatigue or loss of support.
x.Doba spánku a jeho efektivita. Vztahujem: Sleep duration and efficiency. We relate it to your usual amount — an accumulated sleep debt lowers tolerance to load and impairs recovery.
x.Efektivní „plochý ekvivalent\" kilometrů: Effective “flat-equivalent” kilometres over 7 days — distance adjusted for the energy cost of the gradient (Minetti). A hilly run costs more than an equally long flat one, so this number is higher than the real km on rolling terrain. For a jump in load, the Sensitive engine counts terrain cost separately: ascent by energy cost, descent by eccentric load — a steep downhill costs less energy but loads the legs more.
x.Jak jednotvárná byla zátěž v týdnu (vyso: How monotonous the load was during the week (high = almost the same every day, no rest day). High monotony + high volume = “strain”, linked to overload. Ideally alternate hard and easy days.
x.Kadence — počet kroků za minutu. Pokles: Cadence — steps per minute. A drop in cadence at the same pace often comes with fatigue. There's no single right number; what matters is stability against your norm.
x.Kilometry naběhané v klesání od −5 % skl: Kilometres run downhill steeper than −5 % over 7 days. Descent loads the muscles eccentrically (braking) more than its low metabolic cost suggests — so we track it separately. A sharp rise often triggers thigh and knee pain.
x.Klidový tep přes noc. Trvale zvýšený pro: Overnight resting heart rate. Persistently raised against your baseline = the body hasn't recovered (fatigue, stress, illness). A one-off swing doesn't matter; watch the trend.
x.Kolik z vaší zátěže tvoří tvrdé/rychlé b: How much of your load comes from hard/fast runs over 7 days against your norm. An increase in hard sessions raises the risk more than extra kilometres at an easy pace. Interpret it by how much intensity you usually tolerate.
x.Kvalita spánku = podíl hlubokého a REM s: Sleep quality = the share of deep and REM sleep in total sleep, and efficiency (time asleep / time in bed), a 7-night average against your 8-week norm. Deep sleep mainly serves physical recovery, REM the recovery of the nervous system. When the share or efficiency is clearly below your norm, today's readiness goes down — even if you slept long enough. Watches only estimate sleep stages, so quality carries at most half the weight of a signal.
x.Nametrážované klesání (sbíhání) za 7 dní: Measured descent (downhill running) over 7 days in metres. Descent loads the muscles eccentrically more than the flat — so we track it separately. Compare it with “usually”: a sharp jump often triggers knee/thigh pain.
x.Nejtěžší jednotlivý trénink vůči vašemu: The hardest single session against your maximum over the last 30 days — by distance and by intensity (the worse of the two counts). One run clearly bigger than you're used to is the strongest trigger of overload.
x.Odhad délky nejdelšího běhu, který teď z: An estimate of the longest run you can manage now without a big jump in load — derived from your recent history. It serves as a ceiling for planning the weekend long run.
x.Podíl doby kontaktu se zemí na celkové d: The share of ground contact time in the whole stride (duty factor). Lower tends to be a springier, more economical run. It's judged against your baseline at a comparable pace — an increase comes with fatigue.
x.Poměr posledních 7 dní ku vašemu 28denní: The ratio of the last 7 days to your 28-day average. Around ×1.0 means you're running as usual. Well above ×1.3 = a fast increase (riskier); below ×0.8 = easing off or a break. For runners we treat it only as context, not as the main warning.
x.Poměr vertikálního pohybu k délce kroku: The ratio of vertical movement to stride length (%). Lower = a more economical, “flatter” run. What matters is the shift against your baseline at a comparable pace and terrain — a worsening is often a sign of fatigue in your form.
x.Relativní úsilí porovná tepovou zátěž bě: Relative effort compares a run's heart-rate load with your runs of the last 8 weeks (below / usual / above / well above usual). ‘Heart rate at pace’ shows how much higher or lower your heart rate was than you usually need for the same pace — a clearly higher heart rate at an easy pace is often a sign of fatigue, heat or illness.
x.Skóre stavu (0–100): čím vyšší, tím lépe: State score (0–100): the higher, the better. It's 100 minus the risk made up of mechanics, load and symptoms, weighted by the strength of the evidence. 100 = nothing to watch. Above 60 is low risk, 31 to 60 watch, 30 and below high risk. When a safety rule, recurring pain or the load state moves a day into a higher band, its place in the band is set by their severity together with the model. On ordinary days the display brings out even small differences. For each signal we show how many percentage points it takes off the Score. Always against your own history.
x.Součet tréninkové zátěže (běh i jiný spo: The sum of training load (running and other sports) over the last 7 days in load units. The further above your usual week, the bigger the acute load. Watch mainly the jump against previous weeks, not the absolute number.
x.Souhrn stability běžecké formy v čase. K: A summary of how stable your running form is over time. A falling curve = form is breaking down (typically fatigue); stable = you're holding your technique.
x.Spolehlivost — nakolik je už postavená v: Reliability — how far your baseline is built (number of comparable sessions and days of history). While it's low, mechanics signals are better not shown so they don't confuse.
x.Symetrie doby kontaktu levá/pravá (%). I: Left/right ground contact time balance (%). Ideally around 50/50. A growing imbalance may relate to one-sided overload — watch the trend, not a single run.
x.Variabilita tepové frekvence přes noc (m: Overnight heart rate variability (ms). Higher = better recovered. What matters is the deviation from YOUR baseline (in per cent), not the absolute value — a clearer drop against your usual spread suggests fatigue or an oncoming illness.
x.Vertikální oscilace — o kolik se při kaž: Vertical oscillation — how much you “bounce” with each step (cm). Lower tends to be more economical. It's judged against your own runs, not against tables.

x.Připravenost (20–100 %) = jak daleko jso: Readiness (20–100 %) = how far your recovery markers are today from YOUR norm (the last 8 weeks): HRV below the norm and resting heart rate above it — from last night and from the 7-night mean, which is more reliable and counts a quarter more (what the watch shows as HRV status) — shorter sleep than usual (mean of 3 nights) and more time awake at night (sleep efficiency over 3 nights — at most a quarter of a signal, and without confirmation from HRV or resting heart rate only half of that). The share of deep and REM sleep is only shown: watches estimate sleep stages imprecisely and Garmin derives them partly from HRV, so it would count twice. The 7-hour threshold applies only until we know your norm; after that, habitually short sleep is a separate note. Nights under 6 hours always count, even when they are usual for you. The check-in (muscle soreness, fatigue, stress, how you slept) counts towards the Score only under Symptoms, not here. The recommendation in Training still takes it into account as before. A small deviation within your usual day-to-day variation is noise and costs nothing; the bigger the deviation, the lower the readiness. Matching signals add up: when HRV and resting heart rate are each about one of your usual variations off the norm, readiness comes out around 70 %; at almost two, around 40 %; the lowest is 20 %. Readiness reduces capacity (Load) by at most 30 %. After training on the day, readiness drops according to how demanding it was compared with your usual days (an easy session below the first threshold by at most 4 percentage points, a usual day by about 8, your hardest day in 8 weeks by 28, minutes in Z4+ add 8–12, at most 36 in total) — intensity strains recovery more than duration (Stanley et al., 2013; Seiler et al., 2007). The next day, overnight HRV, resting heart rate and sleep replace it; without overnight data, half of a hard session lingers.
